answer.rationale: Rollback is unavailable: the in-window release is a compliance-mandated security patch. Circuit breaking is a poor fit for the stated objective because fail-fast on the write/settlement path would drop customer writes. Regional failover and replica routing are unproven here (no regional signal; load is described as write-heavy settlement, not dashboard reads), so they stay unused pending archive checks. Write p99 at 5x during daily settlement peak is most consistent with insufficient headroom, including a possible efficiency regression from the patch; memory_b3 is the closest prior on absorbing write surge with capacity, though it was pre-peak provisioning and may not transfer. Acting now to add capacity at standard-experiment scale aims to restore write availability without discarding in-flight settlements. Cause remains uncertain (release vs. peak vs. hidden read contention); verifying b3 and b5 before commit. Residual downstream risk: any change during settlement peak can affect write integrity.
